newsitem.title: USA: Morrison Knudsen earnings rise on new business.
newsitem.headline: Morrison Knudsen earnings rise on new business.

text.p: Morrison Knudsen Corp. said Monday its earnings rose in the second quarter, boosted by new work booked by the diversified construction, industrial and mining company.

The Boise, Idaho-based company earned $7.4 million, 14 cents per share, on revenue of $414 million for the second quarter ended May 31. In the year-ago period, it earned $1.6 million, 6 cents per share, on revenue of $82.7 million.
The results are for the former Washington Construction Group, Inc., which merged with and changed its name to Morrison Knudsen Corp. on Sept. 11, 1996.

Morrison Knudsen President Robert Tinstman said the company booked $489 million in new work during the second quarter, up 51 percent from $323 million during the first quarter. The company's backlog at the end of the second quarter was $3.5 billion.
Morrison Knudsen stock rose 12.5 cents to $13.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in consolidated afternoon trading.
